objective: Durably record user directives for the canonical Oya resource model, ORN, Cloud Control Plane, durable operation ledger, mandatory quota/metering/billing resource contract, developer-platform provisioning surface, and Kubernetes/fleet/rollout/billing standards.
implemented_claims: Masterplan session directives now record the Organization -> Account -> Project -> Region -> Cell -> Resource Group -> Resource hierarchy and ORN format.
Platform architecture now distinguishes the user-facing Cloud Control Plane from OpenTofu, Kubernetes Operators, and Argo execution mechanisms.
Platform architecture now records quota service and metering/billing event pipeline as mandatory on every resource type with required resource metadata fields.

Platform architecture now promotes the developer platform/internal console to a core provisioning surface for services, databases, topics, buckets, secrets, SLOs, runbooks, deploy pipelines, and preview environments.

Platform architecture and planning closure now record Cluster API, Gateway API, OpenFeature, FOCUS, OpenCost, and Argo Rollouts/Oya-native equivalent progressive delivery as explicit launch standards.

Platform architecture and planning closure now record that Oya exposes stable cloud resources with lifecycle, identity, policy, quota, billing, audit, observability, rollback, and reconciliation facets.
explicit_non_claims: No stable cloud-resource API contract, lifecycle state machine, identity binding runtime, policy evaluator integration, quota reservation runtime, billing ledger, audit persistence, observability pipeline, rollback controller, or reconciliation controller is implemented by this directive capture.

No Cloud Control Plane API, resource registry service, durable operation ledger persistence, quota service runtime, metering outbox, billing pipeline, developer portal workflow, Cluster API integration, Gateway API deployment, OpenFeature provider, FOCUS/OpenCost exporter, Argo Rollouts runtime, or Oya-native progressive delivery controller is implemented by this ChangeSet.
No OpenTofu plan/apply, Kubernetes API call, Argo CD sync, provider-live operation, FD-001 tenant workload hosting, production readiness, or hyperscaler readiness is claimed.
Full ./bin/oya verify --ci-required is not claimed green unless freshly run and proven.
requirements_recorded: Canonical resource model: Organization -> Account -> Project -> Region -> Cell -> Resource Group -> Resource.
Cloud Control Plane flow: API Gateway -> Resource Registry -> Operation Ledger -> Workflow/Reconciler -> OpenTofu/Operators/Argo.
Every create/update/delete has durable async operation state.
Quota service is reliability infrastructure; quota/metering/billing are mandatory on every resource type.
Every resource type defines quota_cost, billing_meters, audit_events, lifecycle_state, owner, tenant/account/project, region/cell, SLO tier, and deletion/retention policy.
Developer platform/internal console provisions service, database, topic, bucket, secret, SLO, runbook, deploy pipeline, and preview env.
Cluster API, Gateway API, OpenFeature, FOCUS, OpenCost, and explicit progressive delivery via Argo Rollouts or Oya-native equivalent are required standards.
Oya stable cloud resources expose lifecycle, identity, policy, quota, billing, audit, observability, rollback, and reconciliation through the Cloud Control Plane contract.
false_green_findings_closed: Avoided treating OpenTofu modules or Argo templates as the user-facing cloud control plane.
Avoided treating billing/metering as optional future garnish by making the resource contract mandatory in platform architecture.
Avoided treating service catalog/developer portal as docs-only by promoting it to a provisioning surface requirement.
Avoided treating raw IaC/Kubernetes objects as stable Oya cloud resources unless lifecycle, identity, policy, quota, billing, audit, observability, rollback, and reconciliation facets are explicit.

Future ChangeSets needed for Cluster API/Gateway API/OpenFeature/Argo Rollouts or Oya-native progressive delivery implementation.
